name: What is the difference between an in-law suite and an accessory dwelling unit (ADU)?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between an in-law suite and an accessory dwelling unit (ADU)?

acceptedAnswer.text: An in-law suite, or mother-in-law apartment, is an attached or detached living space designed for multigenerational living, often featuring its own bedroom, full bathroom, sitting area, and sometimes a private entrance or kitchenette. In contrast, an accessory dwelling unit (ADU) is typically classified by local zoning codes as an independent secondary housing unit complete with full cooking and sanitation facilities. While homeowners often use these terms interchangeably, local zoning ordinances dictate specific rules regarding setbacks, maximum square footage, utility meters, and whether full kitchens are permitted. Clarifying your household's daily use during initial design helps determine the appropriate legal classification and construction scope.
acceptedAnswer.description: An in-law suite is flexible space for family members, whereas an ADU is legally classified as an independent dwelling unit with distinct zoning rules and full facilities.
